subject: Cloud Computing
title: Block Storage: The Virtual Hard Drive
description: A quick, practical guide to Block Storage: The Virtual Hard Drive.

hook.text: Your cloud server needs a hard drive. Block storage provides one — fast, reliable, and virtual.

buildup.text: Block storage splits data into fixed-size chunks called blocks, each with its own address.

discovery.text: It behaves exactly like a physical hard drive. The operating system can't tell the difference.

twist.text: Block storage is fast but expensive. You pay for allocated space, not just what you actually use.

climax.text: Databases and operating systems run on block storage. It's the performance tier of cloud storage.

punchline.text: Block storage is a virtual hard drive. Same speed, zero shipping.

quiz.question: Why is block storage used for databases in the cloud?
options: It provides fast, low-latency access similar to a physical hard drive
It's the cheapest type of cloud storage available
Databases can only run on block storage by design

details.summary: Block storage provides virtual hard drives that attach to cloud VMs, offering raw storage volumes with low latency and high throughput. Services like AWS EBS and Azure Managed Disks support different performance tiers for workloads ranging from boot volumes to high-IOPS databases.
details.whyItMatters: Block storage is essential for applications that need a traditional file system, like databases and operating systems. Choosing the right volume type directly affects application performance and cost.
takeaways: Block storage provides virtual hard drives for cloud VMs
Different tiers offer varying IOPS and throughput levels
Snapshots enable point-in-time backups of entire volumes

faq.question: How does block storage differ from object storage?
faq.answer: Block storage presents raw volumes that the operating system formats with a file system, offering low latency for random reads and writes. Object storage stores data as complete objects via HTTP APIs. Block storage suits databases and OS disks; object storage suits large-scale unstructured data.

faq.question: What are EBS volume types?
faq.answer: AWS EBS offers gp3 for general purpose, io2 for high-performance databases needing consistent IOPS, st1 for throughput-optimized big data workloads, and sc1 for infrequently accessed cold data. Each type balances performance, durability, and cost differently.
